verses.text: When your leaders spoke, everyone in Israel trembled and showed great respect. But you sinned by worshiping Baal, and you were destroyed.

footnotes.text: your leaders: The Hebrew text has “Ephraim,” here meaning Mount Ephraim, where the royal palace of Samaria (capital of the northern kingdom of Israel) was located.

verses.text: Now you continue to sin by designing and making idols of silver in the shape of calves. You are told to sacrifice to these idols— yes, even to kiss them.

footnotes.text: You are told … idols: One possible meaning for the difficult Hebrew text.

verses.text: And so, all of you will vanish like the mist or the dew of early morning, or husks of grain in the wind or smoke from a chimney.
I, the LORD, have been your God since the time you were in Egypt. I am the only God you know, the only one who can save.
I took care of you in a thirsty desert.

footnotes.text: thirsty desert: The 40 years that Israel wandered through the desert, after leaving Egypt.

verses.text: I fed you till you were satisfied, then you became proud and forgot about me.
Now I will attack like a lion, ambush you like a leopard,
and rip you apart like a bear robbed of her cubs. I will gnaw on your bones, as though I were a lion or some other wild animal.
Israel, you are done for. Don't expect help from me.

footnotes.text: Don't … me: Or “You are against me, the one who helps you.”

verses.text: You wanted a king and rulers. Where is your king now? What cities have rulers?
In my anger, I gave you a king; in my fury, I took him away.
Israel, your terrible sins are written down and stored away.
You are like a senseless child who refuses to be born at the proper time.
Should I, the LORD, rescue you from death and the grave? No! I call death and the grave to strike you like a plague. I refuse to show mercy.
No matter if you prosper more than the other tribes, I, the LORD, will wipe you out, just as a scorching desert wind dries up streams of water. I will take away your precious treasures.

footnotes.text: more … tribes: One possible meaning for the difficult Hebrew text.

verses.text: Samaria will be punished for turning against me. It will be destroyed in war— children will be beaten against rocks, and pregnant women will be ripped open.

footnotes.text: Samaria: The capital of the northern kingdom of Israel.
